name: Lipoma
preview_text: A lipoma is not just a fatty lump - it's a signal from your Spleen and Liver that phlegm and dampness have built up. With herbs, acupuncture, and dietary changes, most people see e...
conventional_description: In conventional medicine, a lipoma is a benign tumor made of fat cells. It usually feels soft, doughy, and moves easily under the skin when pressed. Lipomas are typically painless and grow slowly, often appearing on the trunk, shoulders, neck, or arms. Diagnosis is usually made by physical examination, sometimes confirmed with ultrasound or biopsy if there is any doubt. Most lipomas don't require treatment unless they cause discomfort, restrict movement, or are cosmetically bothersome.
conventional_treatments: The standard approach is watchful waiting. If a lipoma becomes problematic, surgical excision or liposuction can remove it. Recurrence at the same site after complete removal is uncommon, but new lipomas can develop elsewhere. There is no medication to prevent or shrink lipomas.
tcm_understanding:
TCM sees lipomas as “phlegm nodules” - accumulations of thickened, stagnant fluids that have congealed under the skin. The Spleen is the key organ here. It’s responsible for transforming food and drink into usable Qi and for managing fluid metabolism.
When the Spleen is weakened by poor diet, fatigue, or worry, it fails to transport fluids properly. These unprocessed fluids turn into Dampness, which over time thickens into Phlegm. That Phlegm can lodge anywhere in the body; when it settles just beneath the skin, it forms the soft, movable lumps we call lipomas.
But Phlegm isn’t the only culprit. Emotional stress, especially frustration or resentment, can cause Liver Qi to stagnate. Stagnant Qi fails to move Blood and fluids, leading to Phlegm and Blood stasis that makes lipomas firmer and more fixed.
In rare cases, when a lipoma becomes inflamed - red, hot, and painful - it’s because Toxic-Heat has invaded the Phlegm nodule, turning a quiet lump into an acute problem. This is why a single Western diagnosis can have several TCM patterns: a soft, painless lipoma with digestive sluggishness points to Damp-Phlegm or Spleen Deficiency; a firmer, tender lump suggests Qi and Blood Stagnation; a hot, red lump signals Toxic-Heat.
The tongue and pulse give the practitioner a clear window into which pattern is dominant. A thick, greasy tongue coating and slippery pulse confirm Phlegm-Dampness. A pale, swollen tongue with teeth marks points to Spleen weakness. A dark or purple tongue with wiry pulse indicates stagnation. By reading these signs, the practitioner can treat not just the lump but the whole terrain that allowed it to grow.
classical_quote: 「肉瘤者，皮肉间有肉，如指大，不痛不痒，由痰湿凝聚而成。」
classical_translation: "The flesh tumor (Rou Liu) is a growth between the skin and flesh, about the size of a finger, neither painful nor itchy. It is formed by the congealing of phlegm and dampness."
classical_source:
Zhu Bing Yuan Hou Lun (Treatise on the Origins and Symptoms of Diseases)  ,  Volume 31, Section on Flesh Tumors (Rou Liu) 									·

tcm_diagnosis:
A TCM practitioner first examines the lipoma itself - its texture, mobility, and whether it is tender or inflamed - and then looks at the whole person. The most typical presentation is Damp-Phlegm, where the lumps are soft, movable, and painless, often appearing in people with a heavier build. The tongue usually shows a thick white greasy coating and the pulse feels slippery, confirming that phlegm-dampness has congealed under the skin.
If the person also complains of fatigue after eating, bloating, loose stools, and a sallow complexion, the root is likely Spleen Deficiency with Dampness. Here the tongue is pale and swollen with teeth marks, and the pulse is weak. This indicates the Spleen cannot transform fluids properly, so dampness accumulates and eventually hardens into phlegm nodules.
When a lipoma feels firmer, may be tender to the touch, or has been present for a long time, Qi and Blood Stagnation is suspected. The tongue may appear dark or have purple spots, and the pulse is often wiry or choppy. These signs point to a local obstruction of circulation, which can develop after chronic phlegm accumulation or repeated irritation of the lump.
Rarely, a lipoma becomes red, hot, and painful, signaling Toxic-Heat Stagnation. This acute inflammatory picture is accompanied by a red tongue with a yellow coating and a rapid pulse. It demands prompt attention to clear heat and resolve toxins, as it represents a complication rather than the initial cause of the lipoma.

patterns.symptoms: ["Soft, painless, movable lumps under the skin", "Heaviness in the body and limbs", "Poor appetite, bloating, and nausea", "Loose or unformed stools", "Thick, white, greasy tongue coating", "Foggy thinking or muzzy-headedness"]
patterns.worse_with: Greasy, fried, or sweet foods, Cold, raw foods, Damp or humid weather, Sedentary lifestyle, Overeating or irregular meals, Excessive worry or mental strain
patterns.better_with: Light, dry warmth, Gentle daily exercise, Eating warm, cooked grains and vegetables, Avoiding dairy and sugar, Smaller, regular meals
patterns.why_this_happens: When the Spleen is weakened by poor diet or fatigue, it fails to transform fluids properly. These unprocessed fluids accumulate into Dampness, which then thickens and congeals into Phlegm. This Phlegm drifts under the skin and hardens into the soft, movable nodules we call lipomas - essentially, lumps of misplaced body fluid that the system couldn't clear.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale and swollen, often with tooth marks on the sides, coated with a thick, white, greasy fur that looks oily or pasty. Pulse: slippery (滑 huá), rolling smoothly like beads in oil; may also feel soft or soggy at the right middle position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Damp-Phlegm is essentially fluid that has become thick and stagnant because the digestive system (Spleen and Stomach) can't process it. Greasy, sweet, and cold foods directly overwhelm the Spleen, creating more Dampness, while a sedentary lifestyle allows Qi to stagnate so fluids can't be transported. Warmth, gentle movement, and easily digested foods all support the Spleen's function, helping it to dry out existing Phlegm and prevent new nodules from forming.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid cold, raw, greasy, and sweet foods - these are the main culprits that generate Dampness and Phlegm. Favor warm, cooked meals like soups, stews, and lightly steamed vegetables. Gentle daily exercise such as walking or stretching helps move Qi and dry out Dampness. Avoid eating late at night and manage stress, as worry weakens the Spleen.

patterns.why_this_happens: The Spleen is responsible for transforming food into Qi and managing fluids. When it is weak, it fails to do this, and dampness accumulates. Over time, this dampness congeals into phlegm, which then collects under the skin as soft, fatty lumps. This is why lipomas often appear alongside digestive sluggishness and fatigue.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale, swollen body with teeth marks and a white greasy coating. Pulse: soggy (Ru) and slow (Huan), possibly slippery.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: A weak Spleen cannot handle heavy, greasy, or cold foods, which directly create dampness. This dampness thickens into phlegm, forming lipomas. Warm, easily digestible foods and light exercise strengthen the Spleen and help it transport fluids, reducing the phlegm accumulation. Rest and stress management prevent further Qi depletion, allowing the body to clear dampness naturally.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat warm, cooked meals like soups and stews. Avoid cold, raw, greasy, and sweet foods that burden the Spleen and create dampness. Gentle daily exercise such as walking or yoga helps Qi and fluid movement. Keep stress in check, as worry weakens the Spleen.

patterns.why_this_happens: When Qi and Blood circulation become sluggish, especially in the Liver channel, existing phlegm nodules can turn firmer and more fixed. Emotional stress or injury creates local stagnation, leading to a lipoma that feels hard and may ache when pressed. Over time, poor flow causes Blood stasis, which manifests as a dark tongue and a wiry, choppy pulse.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: dark purple body with stasis spots and distended sublingual veins. Pulse: wiry (弦 xián) and choppy (涩 sè).
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Emotional stress directly constricts the Liver Qi, which is responsible for smooth flow of Blood. When Qi stagnates, Blood follows, making lumps harder and more painful. Cold foods and inactivity further congeal Blood, while warmth and gentle movement encourage circulation and help soften the mass. Stress relief allows the Liver to relax, unblocking the stagnation and reducing tenderness.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat warm, cooked foods and avoid icy drinks and raw salads that congeal Qi. Gentle daily movement like walking or stretching helps keep Blood flowing. Manage stress with breathing exercises, as emotional upset directly tightens the Liver Qi and worsens the stagnation.

patterns.why_this_happens:
A lipoma is usually a quiet phlegm-damp nodule, but when toxic heat invades the area - from external infection, dietary overheating, or internal fire - the lump becomes a battleground. Heat and toxins accumulate, causing the nodule to turn red, swell, and feel hot and painful.
This is not how a lipoma starts; it is an acute inflammatory complication. The body’s defensive Qi fights the toxin, which can lead to pus formation if the heat is not cleared.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: deep red or crimson with prickly papillae and a thick, dry yellow coating. Pulse: rapid (shu) and forceful (shi), may be overflowing (hong).
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Toxic heat is a fiery pathogen that flares with heat, spicy foods, and emotional upset. Cooling measures and rest help reduce inflammation by clearing heat and calming the body's internal fire. Avoiding pressure prevents further stagnation and irritation of the nodule.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid spicy, greasy, and fried foods that generate internal heat. Eat cooling foods like mung beans, bitter gourd, cucumber, and watermelon. Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol. Keep the area clean and never squeeze the lump. Gentle activities like walking or meditation help settle the mind and prevent heat from flaring.

formulas.description: A renowned classical formula used to treat red, hot, swollen, and painful skin infections such as boils, abscesses, and inflamed sores in their early stages. It works by clearing the internal Heat driving the infection, improving local blood circulation to reduce swelling and pain, and helping the body expel pus and toxins. Historically called "the foremost formula in external medicine" and "the sacred remedy for abscesses," it is also applied in modern practice for conditions such as mastitis, inflammatory acne, tonsillitis, and appendicitis.

faqs.question: Can TCM dissolve lipomas completely?
faqs.answer: Complete disappearance is possible, especially for smaller, softer lipomas when treated early. For larger or older lumps, the goal is often to shrink them significantly, soften their texture, and prevent new ones from forming. Patience is key - phlegm nodules take time to break down.

faqs.question: Do I need to change my diet?
faqs.answer: Diet is central. Foods that create Dampness and Phlegm - dairy, sugar, greasy fried foods, cold drinks, and excessive raw foods - directly feed the underlying imbalance. Shifting to warm, cooked meals with plenty of vegetables, whole grains, and moderate amounts of lean protein gives the herbs and acupuncture a stronger foundation to work from.

faqs.question: Can I use TCM if I'm considering surgery?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many people use TCM before surgery to try to shrink the lipoma and avoid a procedure. Even if surgery is planned, working on the root imbalance may reduce the chance of new lipomas forming later. Always tell your surgeon and TCM practitioner about all treatments you are receiving.

faqs.question: Is acupuncture painful for lipomas?
faqs.answer: Acupuncture needles are hair-thin and typically cause little discomfort. Some points around the lipoma may be needled to move Qi and Blood locally, but the treatment is gentle. Most people find sessions relaxing.

faqs.question: Are there specific herbs that shrink lipomas?
faqs.answer: No single herb works like a drug. Instead, formulas combine several herbs to address the pattern. For Damp-Phlegm, herbs like Ban Xia (Pinellia) and Chen Pi (Tangerine peel) dry dampness and transform phlegm. For Spleen Deficiency, Bai Zhu (White Atractylodes) and Yi Yi Ren (Job's tears) strengthen the Spleen and drain dampness. A practitioner will prescribe a formula tailored to your pattern.

faqs.question: What if my lipoma suddenly becomes painful?
faqs.answer: Pain, redness, heat, or rapid enlargement could signal inflammation or infection, and you should see a doctor promptly. In TCM, this is often Toxic-Heat invading a Phlegm nodule and requires immediate treatment. Once the acute phase is managed, you can return to the long-term work of clearing phlegm.
